Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Consider leading with experience instead of education.
items.because: The relevant internship may better foreground practical work for the roles you are targeting.

items.says: Use a real, working GitHub or portfolio URL.
Consider adding LinkedIn if you maintain a professional profile.
Clarify whether the 9% booking increase is a relative lift or a percentage-point change.
Ensure the A/B test supports attributing the booking change to your work.
Specify how the JavaScript reduction was measured, if available.
items.because: The metric would be more interpretable.

items.says: Make sure “all 14” refers to issues you personally resolved.
Make clear that the accessibility fixes were verified, not simply implemented.
“Moving image resizing…” is grammatically inconsistent with the surrounding past-tense bullets.
Distinguish the listed optimizations’ contributions if they happened at different times.
items.because: The bullet can sound as though each contributed equally to the score change.

items.says: Lazy-loading the hero image may not explain the claimed LCP improvement.
items.because: A hero image is usually immediately visible, and lazy-loading it can delay its paint.

items.says: Keep this and the Lighthouse result only if they show distinct work and measurements.
Make your contribution or the design-team benefit more concrete if you have evidence.
Converting PNGs to WebP does not ordinarily reduce JavaScript bundle size.
items.because: It ordinarily reduces image-file or page weight instead.

items.says: Clarify the period over which broken-page reports fell from 30 to 6 and confirm the monthly basis.
“Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in August 2024.
Clarify whether the checklist directly caused the audit-failure reduction.
items.because: Other changes may have influenced the result.

items.says: Explain what “search time” measures.
items.because: Technical response time and the time a user takes to find a result imply different impacts.

items.says: Define the measurement period behind “900 riders a week.”
Clarify whether the usage figure counts riders rather than visits or sessions.
The drop from 3.0 to 1.5 seconds is a 50% reduction, not a 75% improvement.
items.because: The incorrect percentage is an easy-to-check inconsistency that can undermine confidence in the metrics.

items.says: Check whether “cold-start” is the right term and specify what the timing includes.
items.because: Caching an offline stop list may improve startup or data availability.

items.says: A rise from 30% to 40% is 10 percentage points, not a 10% relative increase.
items.because: The incorrect percentage terminology can undermine confidence in the metrics.

items.says: State the returning-rider measurement window consistently with “first month.”
Explain how returning riders were measured.
Check whether the increase can be attributed to saved stops.
The heading lists Vue, but the project bullet says React and TypeScript.
items.because: The heading and bullets should consistently identify the framework used for this project.

items.says: Replace “Worked on” with what you specifically owned or delivered.
items.because: The phrase does not show your contribution.

items.says: Include the testing approach or scope if relevant and accurate.
Clarify what the handoff enabled or who used it, if you can support that.
Prioritize technical work or outcomes over the presentation and setup notes if the handoff’s impact cannot be supported.
“Storybok” is misspelled.
“Tools” is not an accurate category for a list of languages and frameworks.
items.because: Grouping skills by type helps recruiters and ATS systems find them.

items.says: The skills list is very short compared with the work shown.
items.because: Relevant languages, testing tools, version control, or web-performance skills could be added if you have used them.
